title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC0LD_1RD1LB_---1RE_0RA1RE_1LA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC0LD_1RD1LB_---1RE_0RA1RE_1LA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced in Lean to a block machine. Lean proves (kernel) that the machine follows an exact block machine and halts if and only if it reaches a left block of exactly four 1s with only single 1s on its right (halts_iff, halts_iff_four), and that every outer configuration 1^N F>0 0 1^3 with N = 2n+4 − 2n − 10 halts (outer_halts). With native_decide: no halt in the first 1.9·1014 steps. Computed: the outer orbit from blank tape is 10, 27, 60, 118, 254, 514, 1014, 2106, 17220, 8534636888060 (about 6.5·1025 steps), never in that set; for N ≤ 3000 the set is exactly where an epoch halts.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The cell rules
claims.text: Fourteen rules for every value of their variables, written by bbtools.symtm.prove: the walk of F over a unit, a round (the left block and the first block that is not a unit each lose two 1s, two units appear), a merge (units, a 0 and the next block become one block 2k + Z + 5), a restart at the left end, the moves at a left block of 2, the endings at the right end, and the halt at a left block of 4.

claims.title: The block machine
claims.text: mstep maps a configuration 0^∞ 1^X F>0 0 (10)^a [mid] (10)^b [tail] (mid nothing, a 0 or an even block, tail nothing or an odd block) to the next with its exact step count; the machine follows it (mstep_sound) and where it says halt the machine halts (mstep_halt). Blank tape reaches 1^10 F>0 0 111 in 102 steps (init_cfg).

claims.title: Halting reduced to the block machine
claims.text: An invariant kept by every macro step excludes the cases the rules do not cover (inv_next); so the machine halts from blank tape iff the block machine reaches halt (halts_iff), iff it reaches a left block of exactly 4 with nothing but units on its right (halts_iff_four).

claims.title: Doubling passes, and where they halt
claims.text: A pass against the block 2q + 3 takes the left block x + 2q + 7 to x + 1 and the block to 2(2q + 4) + 3 (pass); it halts if the left block is 2q + 6 (pass_halt). Hence the outer configuration 1^N F>0 0 1^3 halts for every N = 2n+4 − 2n − 10 (6, 20, 50, 112, 238, 492, ...) (outer_halts).

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.9·10<sup>14</sup> steps
claims.text: 20,000,000 macro steps of the block machine evaluated by compiled code, with the runner proved to be a run of the machine: no halt in the first 191,906,825,348,151 steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps, directly
claims.text: The list simulator from blank tape (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone).

claims.title: The block machine agrees with the machine
claims.text: py/macro.py check 1e8 compares the whole tape and the step count at each of the 15,261 macro configurations of the first 108 steps with the block machine: all agree.

claims.title: The outer orbit
claims.text: With rounds batched and inner epochs jumped by their closed form (checked for every j < 400): from blank tape the outer configurations are N = 10 (step 102), 27, 60, 118, 254, 514, 1014, 2106 (step 2,911,484), 17220 (step 251,528,266) and 8534636888060 (about 6.54·10<sup>25</sup> steps). None is of the form 2<sup>n+4</sup> − 2n − 10.

claims.title: Where an epoch halts
claims.text: For 5 ≤ N ≤ 3000 the epoch from 1^N F>0 0 1^3 halts iff N = 2n+4 − 2n − 10 for some n; otherwise it reaches the next outer configuration.

claims.title: The inner epochs
claims.text: After the doubling passes the units in front of a stored block feed inner epochs: X<sub>j</sub> = 24·2<sup>j</sup> − 3 becomes X<sub>j+1</sub>, using j + 4 units, in 1152·4<sup>j</sup> − 216·2<sup>j</sup> + 10 steps. Found from the run and checked for j < 400, not proved; so N' is about 2<sup>c√N</sup> with c about 1/3.

claims.title: Why it probably never halts
claims.text: The halting set has one element per doubling of N, so a random N of its size lies in it with chance about 1/N; the orbit is already at 8.5·10<sup>12</sup> and grows doubly exponentially, so the chance of a later hit is negligible.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: it halts iff the outer orbit hits 2n+4 − 2n − 10 (the if direction proved in Lean, the converse computed for N ≤ 3000). The map N → N' depends on the remainder of the doubling passes, a Collatz-like question.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but the question has been boiled down. This machine is a doubly exponential counter: a block of 1s on the left and blocks on the right wear each other down two by two, units merge into blocks twice as big, and each epoch 1^N F>0 0 1^3 leads to a new one with N about 2√N/3. Lean proves it halts exactly when a left block of four meets nothing but single 1s, which happens when N is one of 6, 20, 50, 112, 238, ... = 2n+4 − 2n − 10. The orbit 10, 27, 60, ..., 17220, 8534636888060 has missed them all.

facts.text: Halts iff the block machine reaches a left block of four with only units on its right (Lean, kernel).
No halt, proved in Lean by running the block machine.
The 9th outer configuration, at about 6.5·10<sup>25</sup> steps, is not in the halting set.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.439). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 41,641 cells (29,240 left of the start, 138 right), with a density of 1s of 0.754.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: At every macro configuration the head is in state F on a gap 0 0. Left of it is one block of X ones, with blank tape beyond. Right of it is a row of blocks of 1s, each followed by one 0: first a run of units (single 1s), then at most one even block or an extra 0, more units, and at most one odd block at the end:
0^∞ 1^X F>0 0 (1 0)^a [mid] (1 0)^b [tail] 0^∞

F walks over a unit in two steps, so the units are free to travel between the gap and the first real block. Lean's Q = ⟨X, a, mid, b, tail⟩ names this shape, and mstep says what comes next, with the exact number of steps.

sections.heading: Rounds and merges
html: A round. With k units in front of a block Y ≥ 2 and X ≥ 3, the head goes over and back: the left block and the block both lose two 1s, and two new units appear.

So against an odd block 2q + 3, q + 1 rounds use it up into 2q + 3 units, which then merge into the block 2(2q + 3) + 5: a doubling pass that costs the left block 2q + 6 ones (pass). When the left block runs out, a restart carries units and a block back to the left end as the new left block.

sections.heading: A doubly exponential counter
html: An epoch starts at an outer configuration O(N) = 1^N F>0 0 1^3. First the right block doubles again and again (3, 11, 27, 59, ...) while eating N. What is left of N becomes a stock of units in front of a stored block. Then come inner epochs: the left block is 24·2j − 3 (21, 45, 93, ...), a small block doubles through 6, 18, 42, ..., eating one unit per merge, and a restart doubles the left block. Each inner epoch uses j + 4 units. When the units are gone, everything merges and the epoch ends at O(N').
With u units there are about √(2u) inner epochs, so N' is about 2√(2u), roughly 2√N/3. From blank tape:

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The machine halts only when the left block is exactly four 1s and the right side holds nothing but units: D then reads a blank (halts_iff_four). In an epoch that happens when a doubling pass leaves exactly four 1s. Adding up the passes 3, 11, 27, ..., this is exactly when
N = 2n+4 − 2n − 10   = 6, 20, 50, 112, 238, 492, 1002, 2024, ...

Lean proves that each of these halts (outer_halts); for every N up to 3000 they are the only epochs that halt. The orbit came close (118 next to 112, 2106 near 2024) but never hit. These targets get exponentially sparse while N grows doubly exponentially, so a hit looks ever less likely, but nothing proves that the orbit avoids them.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Kernel: the 14 cell rules; the block machine and its soundness (mstep_sound, mstep_halt); halts_iff and halts_iff_four; the doubling pass and outer_halts.
native_decide: no halt in the first 191,906,825,348,151 steps (blank_runs_macro).

Computed: the block machine agrees with the machine on 108 steps; the outer orbit up to 8534636888060; the halting set for N ≤ 3000. Not proved: the inner-epoch formula in general, and whether the orbit ever hits the halting set.

family: doubly exponential counter; halts iff the outer orbit hits 2^(n+4) - 2n - 10
summary: A left block of 1s and blocks on the right wear each other down two by two, and units merge into doubled blocks; epochs O(N) = 1^N F>0 0 1^3 go to O(N') with N' about 2^(√N/3). Proved in Lean: it halts iff the block machine reaches a left block of four with only units on its right, and O(N) halts for every N = 2^(n+4) - 2n - 10; the orbit 10, 27, 60, ..., 17220, 8534636888060 never hits that set.
